results.snippet: 1. Why a Retried POST Can Run Twice. A request is idempotent when sending it several times leaves the server in the same state as sending it once. Section 9.2.2 of RFC 9110, the HTTP specification, gives this property to PUT, DELETE and the safe methods such as GET.

results.title: HTTP Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
results.snippet: GET and HEAD are safe; POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE are not. Idempotent: A method is idempotent if multiple identical calls have the same effect on the server as a single one. According to RFC 9110, PUT, DELETE, and all safe methods (GET, HEAD) are idempotent.

provider_calls.text:
按照 HTTP 规范（现行的 RFC 9110，此前为 RFC 7231 / RFC 2616），**幂等性（Idempotence）**指的是：**多个完全相同的请求对服务器产生的预期效果（状态影响），与单个请求所产生的效果是一致的**。

规范对 `PUT` 和 `POST` 的保证和语义定义差异很明确：

### 1. `PUT`：规范明确保证为幂等方法（Idempotent）
* **语义定义**：`PUT` 要求请求载荷替换目标资源的当前状态（或在目标 URL 处新建该资源）。
* **重复请求的效果**：如果连续发送多个完全相同的 `PUT` 请求，除了可能产生的统计或审计日志等无状态副作用外，服务器上该资源的最终状态与只执行一次是一模一样的。
* **客户端与中间件行为**：因为规范定义了其幂等性，当网络中断、超时或遇到连接重置时，用户代理（浏览器/客户端）或中间代理通常可以在无需用户再次确认的情况下**安全地自动重试**。
* **注意响应状态码不要求完全一致**：幂等性衡量的是**服务器端的副作用与状态**，而不是响应体或状态码。例如第一次 `PUT` 可能会返回 `201 Created`，重复发送时返回 `200 OK` 或 `204 No Content`，这依然完全符合幂等规范。

### 2. `POST`：规范定义为非幂等方法（Non-idempotent）
* **语义定义**：`POST` 用于让目标资源根据其自身的特定语义来处理请求载荷（如新增从属条目、提交表单、发送指令等）。
* **重复请求的效果**：规范**不保证**其幂等性。每重复执行一次请求，服务器通常都会产生新的累积副作用（例如生成一条新订单、追加一条数据库记录）。
* **客户端与中间件行为**：规范要求用户代理在重复发送 `POST` 请求时必须保持谨慎。如果网络中断导致结果未知，客户端**不能**擅自静默自动重试；如果需要重新提交，通常必须向用户提示确认（比如浏览器刷新页面时常见的“重新提交表单”弹窗）。

---

### 需要注意的现实与实现边界
规范层面的保证实质上是一种**协议契约**：
* 协议规范负责给出语义预期。如果服务端接口把 `PUT` 实现成了每次请求数值加一，或者让其产生非幂等副作用，那就是服务端的实现违背了 HTTP 规范，破坏了客户端与代理缓存的合理假设。
* 同样地，如果业务上确实需要 `POST` 实现重复请求的安全重试，HTTP 协议本身并不提供原生保证，必须在应用层引入机制配合（例如常见的 `Idempotency-Key` 幂等键或唯一交易号机制）来解决。

# RFC 9110
# HTTP Semantics
## [Abstract](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#abstract)
The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is a stateless application-level protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypertext information systems. This document describes the overall architecture of HTTP, establishes common terminology, and defines aspects of the protocol that are shared by all versions. In this definition are core protocol elements, extensibility mechanisms, and the "http" and "https" Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) schemes.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-abstract-1)
This document updates RFC 3864 and obsoletes RFCs 2818, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694, and portions of 7230.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-abstract-2)

It has received public review and has been approved for publication by the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG). ###  [1.1. ](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-1.1)[Purpose](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-purpose)
The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is a family of stateless, application-level, request/response protocols that share a generic interface, extensible semantics, and self-descriptive messages to enable flexible interaction with network-based hypertext information systems.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-1.1-1)
HTTP hides the details of how a service is implemented by presenting a uniform interface to clients that is independent of the types of resources provided. Likewise, servers do not need to be aware of each client's purpose: a request can be considered in isolation rather than being associated with a specific type of client or a predetermined sequence of application steps. This allows general-purpose implementations to be used effectively in many different contexts, reduces interaction complexity, and enables independent evolution over time.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-1.1-2)
HTTP is also designed for use as an intermediation protocol, wherein proxies and gateways can translate non-HTTP information systems into a more generic interface.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-1.1-3)
One consequence of this flexibility is that the protocol cannot be defined in terms of what occurs behind the interface. Instead, we are limited to defining the syntax of communication, the intent of received communication, and the expected behavior of recipients. provider_calls.text:
在 HTTP 规范（如 RFC 9110 第 9.2 节）中，“幂等性”（Idempotent）的定义是：**对同一个资源执行多次相同请求，在服务器端产生的预期状态效果，与执行单次请求是完全一致的**。

关于 PUT 和 POST，规范层面的保证与差异主要体现在这几个方面：

### 1. 规范对方法的语义定义
* **PUT 是幂等的（Idempotent）**：
  * PUT 的语义是用请求体中的内容完整创建或替换目标 URI 对应的资源状态。
  * 连续发送多次完全相同的 `PUT /items/1`，无论执行 1 次还是 10 次，该资源在服务器上的最终状态都是相同的。
  * **注意响应状态码不要求完全一样**：规范定义的幂等性针对的是服务器的状态副作用，而不是响应消息。例如第一次 PUT 可能返回 `201 Created`，随后的重复请求可能返回 `200 OK` 或 `204 No Content`，这依然满足幂等。
* **POST 是非幂等的（Non-idempotent）**：
  * POST 的语义是让目标资源根据自身逻辑处理请求负载，通常用于追加数据、创建从属资源或执行非幂等的业务动作（如转账、提交订单）。
  * 连续发送多次相同的 POST 请求，服务器可能会创建多个新资源（生成不同 ID）或重复执行业务逻辑，产生累积副作用。

### 2. 客户端重试（Retry）与网络异常处理的规范行为
规范对自动重试有明确的安全指导：
* **PUT 请求**：如果在传输中连接中断或超时，客户端和中继代理在规范上被允许自动发起重试，因为多次到达不会产生额外的业务副作用。
* **POST 请求**：客户端或代理**不得**在未征得用户确认的情况下自动重新提交未完成的请求，避免引起重复扣款或重复发帖等问题。

### 3. 规范保证与实现落地的边界
* **协议层只是“语义契约”**：HTTP 规范规定了方法的设计意图，但协议本身无法从底层强制业务代码如何编写。如果服务端在处理 PUT 时在数据库里写了自增计数，那就违反了 HTTP 语义约定。
* **POST 实现幂等需要应用层协议**：如果业务需要在 POST 下实现幂等（例如重试防重），需要依赖应用层机制，比如由客户端附带 `Idempotency-Key` 请求头、业务唯一流水号或数据库唯一约束来实现。

你是在设计接口规范，还是在排查网络重试导致的重复提交问题呢？

results.snippet: 1. Why a Retried POST Can Run Twice. A request is idempotent when sending it several times leaves the server in the same state as sending it once. Section 9.2.2 of RFC 9110, the HTTP specification, gives this property to PUT, DELETE and the safe methods such as GET.

results.snippet: There are nine methods defined by RFC 9110: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, OPTIONS, TRACE, and PATCH (PATCH is defined separately in RFC 5789). Most APIs use five or six.

results.snippet: POST — Non-Idempotent Creation and Actions. PUT — Full Replacement. PATCH — Partial Update. DELETE and OPTIONS.RFC 9110 explicitly discourages defining custom HTTP methods. Instead: Use a standard method + differentiate by URL (POST /actions/approve).

results.title: HTTP Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
results.snippet: GET and HEAD are safe; POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE are not. Idempotent: A method is idempotent if multiple identical calls have the same effect on the server as a single one. According to RFC 9110, PUT, DELETE, and all safe methods (GET, HEAD) are idempotent.

## [Abstract](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#abstract)

The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is a family of stateless, application-level, request/response protocols that share a generic interface, extensible semantics, and self-descriptive messages to enable flexible interaction with network-based hypertext information systems.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-1.1-1)
